previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic abdominal pain, gastroparesis, and vulvodynia was admitted for severe epigastric pain and nausea, consistent with prior chronic pancreatitis flares. Labs showed only mild lipase elevation, ruling out acute pancreatitis. She was managed with IV fluids, pain control using IV then oral hydromorphone, and gradual advancement to a regular diet. A gastric emptying study confirmed markedly delayed emptying (81% retention at 4 hours), and she was transitioned from metoclopramide to erythromycin, with dose adjustment due to diarrhea. Her anxiety, depression, and hearing impairment were accommodated throughout. She improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with a plan to follow up with gastroenterology and taper narcotics to reduce future hospitalizations.
